chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hareez, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
He was asked about what is killed by the stone and the pellet — can one eat from it? He said: No.

key_terms.البندق: Pellet/bunduk — a round, non-sharp projectile fired from a sling or early firearm
key_terms.الحجر: Stone — a blunt projectile used as a thrown weapon
key_terms.يُؤكل: Is it eaten/permissible to eat — a standard fiqh inquiry about halal status

ai.seo_question: Is game killed by a stone or pellet permissible to eat in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked a jurisprudential question about game animals killed by non-penetrating projectiles such as stones or pellets (bunduk). His response was unequivocal: such game is not permissible to eat. In Islamic jurisprudence, for hunted game to be lawful, it must be killed by a weapon that causes penetrating injury (dhabh or hunting with sharp instruments), not by blunt force which amounts to a stunning blow.
